# Exact task and command contract

Task manifest, task-command registry, review-command registry, cybersecurity registry, ownership registry, command I/O registry and negative-vector file form one semantic validation input. P00 and P02 must use all of them. The bundled plan_tools/check_plan.py provides the executable declaration-level reference behavior; runtime validators implement the same counterexamples after materialization.

Reject production authority; duplicate task/command/path IDs; unknown or forward dependencies; task-count mismatch; unapproved lifecycle regression; empty or whitespace-only rollback; unowned outputs, tests, symbols, command inputs and registry consumers; consumers preceding owners; missing schema pointers; and placeholder commands. Reject exact tokens TODO, TBD, FIXME, PLACEHOLDER, ..., angle-bracket slots, shell expansion ${...} or $(...), and backticks in executable paths/arguments. Literal code supplied to python -c is allowed only for BOOT0_EXTRACT_PLAN and must byte-match the supplied extractor; it is not interpolated by a shell. Prompts may appear only as data inputs, never as argv[0] or script entrypoints.

A command is one exact argv array, cwd and closed access policy. An operation command is not proof merely because expected_exit is zero. Candidate replay uses only the exact command IDs in verification-topology.v1.json; it excludes the registry runner itself, future export/seal operations, host-key bootstrap, review launches and crash-child subcommands already invoked by their registered parent harness. Expected intentional-red inherited discovery contracts are classified separately and cannot satisfy v6.3.6 tooling proof.
